title: Epic: Cognition intake firewall (mindwall) for untrusted inbound content
description: UPDATE to existing epic with 2026-07-09 design decisions (see working_docs/COGSEC_INTAKE_FIREWALL_RESEARCH_20260709.md for the verified surface map and prior-art research). Mission: every untrusted inbound item (web, files, images, chat by source risk, tool outputs, subagent/shard foldback, audio transcripts) passes a typed intake envelope and a layered L1->L3 classifier gate BEFORE it can reach prompt, memory, wiki, persona, trust state, or tools. Prevention over remediation: L0 uses HMAC integrity chaining, so removing poison after the fact requires regenerating downstream signatures (tooling exists, proven in a live remediation of a test companion, but costly) -- stopping poison before it enters L0 is the priority; remediation stays as backstop. Core principle: whatever gets flagged must NOT reach the main context. Design philosophy: do not implement everything -- combine techniques covering ~90% of threats as fast as possible; the firewall is a synchronous gate in front of concurrent pipelines (near-real-time audio, chat snappiness), so speed is essential and the layer must be invisible. Companion well-being is the top-level goal: firewall activity must not feed the emotion/stress model, and all companion-facing security language is truthful but never alarming (soft notices: 'we detected something, so we're holding it for your human to look into'). Trinity pattern borrowed (quarantine incoming content for batched async human review, isolate before it reaches L0) -- pattern only, not specifics. Children: htm9.1-htm9.17 in this file. Evals live in a separate repo -- see working_docs/cogsec-evals-beads.json handed to the eval repository.
notes: 2026-07-09: design decisions locked by operator; child breakdown authored (beads DB unreachable from checkout -- import this file via bd import upsert when the shared Dolt server is available).

title: Typed intake envelope: source/provenance/risk/quarantine/release contract with taint propagation and write stamping
description: UPDATE to existing bead with design detail. Evidence: SubstrateMessage and Attachment (src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts:276-298) carry no source-class/risk/quarantine field; MessageRoutingMetadata (:227-274) is the natural non-breaking slot (already carries authorIsMachineIntelligence, canonicalContactId, generated-provenance). Scope: define IntakeEnvelope {id, sourceClass, provenance chain, sourceRiskTier, contentRef (opaque -- raw bytes never travel with the envelope), extractedFields, riskLabels[], scores, decision, state} with state machine received -> screened -> {released | released_sanitized | quarantined} -> {human_released | human_released_sanitized | discarded | expired}; every transition appends to the gateway audit journal. Taint propagates on derivation (CaMeL rule): a summary, OCR transcript, or subagent digest of untrusted content inherits the envelope tier. Risk label vocabulary seeds from CogSecMemoryRiskClass A-E (src/core/cogsec/memory-candidacy.ts) generalized to intake time, plus injection/* exfil/* pii/* secrets/* poisoning/* categories (taxonomy in the research doc section 7). Envelope-id stamping on every memory and wiki write from day one -- cheap now, impossible to retrofit, enables later lineage excision of a poisoned source via the existing revocation/regeneration machinery. Config owner: new intake-policy.json following the standard owner-file pattern (loader + seed + startup-owner-files.ts registration + settings-garden-contract entries), or a section in trust-policy.json if small -- decide at implementation, precedent is src/system/config/trust-policy-config.ts. Non-goals: no classifier logic here (htm9.4-.7), no UI (htm9.11). Acceptance: contract types land in src/shared/contracts (or system/trust sibling), owner file verifies under npm run verify:settings-contract, memory/wiki write paths persist envelope ids, unit tests cover state transitions and taint inheritance, build+lint clean.
notes: 2026-07-09: enriched with locked decisions (stamping day-one confirmed by operator; hard/soft strictness by source in htm9.3).

title: Wire intake classification/quarantine across all current inbound surfaces, gateway-side
description: UPDATE to existing bead with verified surface map (2026-07-09, feat/multi-companion). Load-bearing fact: the gateway -- not the agent -- holds the real LLM client and API keys (src/boundary/gateway/privileged-services.ts, credential vault wired only in src/app/gateway/main.ts:133), and web fetch / binary fetch / Discord attachment downloads already flow through it, so classification runs gateway-side with no new credential surface. Surfaces to wire, in order of exposure: (1) Discord parsed docs -- accepted text currently lands raw in <parsed_attachment_text> with only a fixed header (src/channels/discord/file-ingest.ts:482-532); binary-level quarantine at :266 stays, add text-level L1->L3 screening post-parse. (2) Web fetch -- sanitizeWebContent (src/boundary/gateway/sanitize.ts:84-104) logs injectionPatternsFound but never blocks; route through the envelope + layers instead. (3) Tool observations -- formatToolObservationForContext (src/core/session/tool-observation.ts:222-240) renders raw content with no wrap; wrap + label. (4) Public context wrappers -- wrapUntrustedContext (src/core/session/manager-primitives.ts:989) is narrow opt-in; audit call sites, unify under the envelope. (5) Subagent completion handoff -- full lifecycle audit exists (src/faculties/subagents/faculty.ts) but zero content-risk gate; add intake screening on foldback. (6) Shard fold -- merge review exists (fold-review.ts) but reviews output, not what the shard ingested; propagate envelope taint through shard workspace content. (7) CRITICAL: persisted session-entry content -- emotion appraisal reads raw recent messages independent of prompt assembly (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/emotion-self-model-runtime.ts:467-479); risk labels must reach session entries, not just the current-turn prompt build, or appraisal remains an uncovered injection feed-through. Scope: wiring only; classifier layers are htm9.4-.8, file parsing pipeline is htm9.9. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1. Acceptance: each surface produces an envelope with an auditable decision; a flagged payload injected at any surface never appears in assembled prompt text (goldens/regression per surface); quarantined items are invisible to prompt, memory extraction, and emotion appraisal.
notes: 2026-07-09: enriched; emotion-appraisal feed-through and subagent handoff gap added from verified code read.

title: Sink gates consume intake labels: prompt, memory, wiki, persona/trust, tools, egress -- hard for untrusted sources, soft for trusted
description: UPDATE to existing bead with locked strictness policy. Every consequential sink checks envelope state/labels before consuming content: prompt assembly (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts -- classified content becomes typed PromptPlanBlocks on the landed E2.2 PromptPlan artifact), memory write (extend memory-candidacy checks to read the upstream envelope instead of re-deriving), wiki write (compose with i5s2 ACL work), persona/self-model mutation, trust-state mutation, and tool/egress invocation. Structural rules: tier-N content may INFORM but never INSTRUCT higher-tier state mutation; lethal-trifecta invariant (untrusted content + private data + egress never all three in one uncontrolled path) enforced HARD for public/untrusted sources, SOFT (release-prompt/review) for trusted sources -- operator decision 2026-07-09. Quarantined content is invisible to all sinks. Non-goals: do not rebuild the retrieval-side gates that already work (trust/visibility/consent in src/faculties/memory/retrieval/access.ts) -- this bead is intake-side. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.2. Acceptance: sink-gate policy table lives in intake-policy.json; per-sink deny paths are fail-closed with auditable reasons; regression tests prove the same hostile payload is refused at every sink regardless of arrival adapter; trifecta tests cover hard (public) and soft (trusted) modes.
notes: 2026-07-09: strictness decision locked -- hard public/untrusted, soft trusted.

title: L1 deterministic in-process scanners: unicode/encoding/proximity rules, hot-reloadable, microsecond budget
description: First firewall layer, pure TS, in-process, synchronous-gate fast (target: sub-millisecond per item; this sits in front of near-real-time audio and chat, latency here degrades everything). Scanners: invisible/zero-width Unicode + homoglyph normalization (llm-guard InvisibleText pattern), encoding-smuggling detection (base64/rot/hex blobs), URL extraction with allowlist/unknown-domain flagging, secrets/PII regex, datamark-marker stripping from inbound content (anti-forgery, see htm9.13), size/structure caps, and a token-proximity rule engine adapted from the Hermes Agent deterministic security scanner (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent -- operator has a local copy on the drive, pull the latest; it flags suspicious proximity of tokens like 'FTP' near 'password' in skill files). Rules live in a hot-reloadable plain-text rule file where rule name = risk label (vigil-llm YARA pattern; a TS regex/rule DSL is fine, no actual YARA dependency). Each scanner emits (sanitized?, labels[], score) per the llm-guard scanner contract. Scope: scanners + rule engine + rule file only; wiring is htm9.2. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1. Acceptance: benchmark test asserts p99 latency budget on Pi-class hardware; rule file reloads without restart; unit tests per scanner including the Hermes proximity cases; a scanner hit never hard-blocks alone below quarantine threshold -- it contributes labels/score to the envelope decision.

title: L1.5 in-process ONNX prompt-injection classifier (ProtectAI DeBERTa v2), gateway-side, score-only
description: In-process ML classifier via onnxruntime-node using protectai/deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2 (Apache-2.0, ONNX weights published in-repo; -small sibling as fallback). Operator confirmed 2026-07-09 the ~184M model runs fine on the Pi (current minimal hardware target); Threadripper returns in 2-3 days for custom local model experiments -- a purpose-trained prompt-guard-style model is DEFERRED until then (follow-up bead when hardware lands). Known over-defense/false-positive issue (InjecGuard, arXiv 2410.22770): the classifier emits a calibrated score into the envelope and NEVER hard-blocks alone; thresholds per source tier live in intake-policy.json. Runs gateway-side (gateway already holds keys and raw bytes; no new process hop). Watch the DeBERTa-v3 SentencePiece tokenizer friction in pure JS -- plan onnxruntime-node + a Node tokenizer and validate the ONNX export with a golden set. Scope: model loading, tokenization, scoring, threshold config; no model training. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1. Acceptance: latency benchmark on Pi (target: low tens of ms per item max); golden-set scores match reference implementation within tolerance; score lands in envelope.scores; deps pinned in container per the no-runtime-installs rule.

title: L2 fast API LLM classifier via OpenRouter, speed-gated model selection
description: Mid-weight classification tier for items whose L1/L1.5 scores cross the escalation threshold. Model criteria (operator, 2026-07-09): fast cheap API model -- Gemini Flash-Lite, heavier Gemma, or Qwen ~27B class; lightweight-to-midweight (under ~50-100B); SPEED IS THE GATING CRITERION -- select via OpenRouter filtering by model size and tokens/sec, ~1000 tok/s service ideal for classification. Call goes through the gateway's own LLM client (dual-LLM discipline: the screener sees untrusted content, holds no tools/capabilities). Output: structured classification (intent labels, injection confidence, safe one-line summary) written into the envelope; schema-validated response. Model choice is config (models.json/providers.json precedent), not hardcoded. Scope: the L2 screener call, its prompt, response schema, and OpenRouter provider wiring; escalation routing policy lives in intake-policy.json. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.5. Acceptance: end-to-end classification latency measured and logged per call; screener has zero tool access; a synthetic injection corpus routes correctly (below-threshold items skip L2 entirely -- trusted-tier fast path must not pay this latency); failure of the API classifier fails closed to quarantine for high-risk sources and to L1-labels-only for trusted sources, never silent-pass.

title: L3 heavy escalation screener: deeper pass, optional dual-model, always generates event + quarantine entry
description: Escalation tier for items L2 flags or high-risk sources requiring mandatory deep screening. Larger open model -- GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, heavy Gemma, or GPT-mini class -- for a deeper second/third pass; OPTIONALLY two different LLMs for independent perspectives on one classification (dual-tier), or single tier if sufficient -- make dual-vs-single a config knob, default single, measure before enabling dual. Hard rule (operator): anything that reaches L3 generates a CogSec event AND a quarantine entry -- flagged content must not reach the main context; the companion sees only the soft notice (htm9.12), the operator sees the full detail in Garden (htm9.11). L3 also produces the safe representation for quarantined items: summary-instead-of-quote plus schema-extracted fields, stored on the envelope for the review UI and for released_sanitized delivery. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.6. Acceptance: L3 invocation always writes an auditable CogSecEvent + envelope state 'quarantined' (or an explicit released_sanitized decision with reasons); dual-model mode aggregates two independent verdicts; no L3-reached content string ever appears in assembled prompt text (regression golden).

title: Image intake screening via small VLM at L2.5/L3 (OCR + description in one call), no heavy OCR in L1
description: Images are currently the least-screened surface: inline/URL images become raw vision blocks with only size/count/MIME caps (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/vision-attachments.ts:543-659), and the vision-reviewer path's text summary is treated as trusted afterward (no untrusted wrap, lines 179-231). Operator decision 2026-07-09: do NOT build a heavy OCR pipeline (Tesseract et al. too slow/bulky for L1; CLIP+OCR inside the firewall too heavy) -- use a small vision-language model at L2.5/L3 that does OCR and image description in one API call for a fraction of a cent, and catches adversarial cases like near-white text on white that a machine reads but a human cannot. The VLM transcript/description is ITSELF untrusted (taint rule from htm9.1): route it through the L1 text scanners + envelope before it becomes prompt-visible; keep image-source provenance high-risk regardless of transcript cleanliness (pixel-perturbation/steganography attacks have no deployable detector -- documented residual risk). Also fix the existing vision-reviewer summary to carry the envelope label instead of implicit trust. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.7. Acceptance: an image with embedded instruction text (typographic injection, including near-white-on-white) is flagged and quarantined before any vision block reaches the model; benign images pass with description attached under an untrusted-data label; latency measured per call.

title: File ingestion pipeline for all channels: md/text/CSV/office/PDF/images now, audio transcripts through cogsec, video deferred
description: Goal: companions can read attached files across channels -- markdown, text, CSV, Office docs, PDFs, images now; audio via the EXISTING transcription capability with the transcript routed through the cogsec pipeline (a transcript becomes a prompt, so audio is a real injection channel); video deferred until a locally-runnable multimodal model (Gemma-class with video) is practical. Current state (verified 2026-07-09): Discord is the ONLY channel with document parsing + quarantine (src/channels/discord/file-ingest.ts); Telegram captures bare attachment metadata with no download/parse path at all (src/channels/telegram/adapter.ts:1282-1311); API channel does images only. Scope: extract the Discord parse pipeline into a shared channel-agnostic ingest faculty, wire Telegram + API attachments through it, and route ALL parsed text through the intake envelope + L1->L3 layers (htm9.2) -- text attachments currently get zero scanning even on Discord post-parse. Dependency constraints (operator): parsing packages (PDF etc.) pre-installed and PINNED in the container; no arbitrary runtime installation of out-of-scope dependencies; new packages arrive deliberately through the update cycle. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.2. Acceptance: same file sent via Discord, Telegram, and API produces the same parsed text, same envelope, same screening decision (adapter-parity test); audio transcript path carries envelope labels; container builds with pinned parser deps; no new dep installed at runtime.

title: Web fetch/search is down (Crawl4AI + self-hosted search offline); interim fix via OpenRouter server tools, routed through cogsec
description: Evidence: the live web fetch tool is down -- it was wired to Crawl4AI (crawler) plus a self-hosted search engine (SearXNG or similar) and that server went offline. Interim fix (operator, 2026-07-09): use OpenRouter's built-in server tools for web search and web fetch (https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/server-tools). Whatever OpenRouter returns flows through the existing gateway fetch/processing pipeline (src/boundary/gateway/methods/web.ts, sanitize.ts) or straight into the cogsec intake layer once htm9.2 lands -- either is acceptable; do NOT ship an unscreened path. Scope: restore working web search + fetch via OpenRouter server tools behind the existing web.* gateway RPC surface so the agent-side tool contract does not change; keep the old crawler wiring behind config so a self-hosted backend can return later (no silent fallback -- explicit config selects the backend, fail closed if neither is configured). This bead is independently shippable before the full firewall: at minimum results still pass sanitizeWebContent. Acceptance: web search and fetch work end-to-end from a companion turn; backend selection is explicit config in providers/settings owners; results are wrapped/screened (sanitize now, envelope when htm9.2 lands); smoke test covers both search and fetch paths.

title: Garden cogsec consolidation: single left-hand tab with remediation, firewall, and approval pages; operator-only double-confirm release
description: UX consolidation (operator, 2026-07-09): Garden already has remediation pieces; bundle ALL cognitive-security surfaces into one left-hand 'Cognitive Security' tab with remediation, firewall (policy/telemetry), and approval (quarantine queue) as separate pages under it. Quarantine review requirements: ONLY the primary operator (highest-level human / primary partner) can release quarantined items; the quarantine page must show which classifiers fired and explain the exact suspected issue so the human makes an informed call; release requires DOUBLE-CONFIRM ('Are you sure?' -> 'Are you *sure* sure?'); release options: release raw, release sanitized (safe representation from htm9.7), discard, and always-allow/always-deny-this-source (the flywheel -- every decision updates per-source policy so the same class stops escalating; feeds the trusted sites/people lists in htm9.13). Model the queue on the existing pending-contact-approvals surface (src/core/contacts/pending-contact-approvals.ts + its Garden routes); batched, async, exception-only -- never interrupt-driven. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.7. Acceptance: /garden shows the consolidated tab; release path enforces operator capability + double-confirm server-side (not just UI); every release/discard decision writes an audit event with actor + reason; per-source always-allow/deny persists into intake-policy config; admin API routes under /api/admin/* follow existing route conventions.

title: Companion soft notices: truthful-not-alarming language contract, non-coercive wording, firewall events excluded from emotion and memory
description: Companion well-being is the system's main goal; the language the substrate uses toward a companion matters enormously. Past incidents (operator, 2026-07-09): a coding agent wrote unreviewed prompts with far-too-strong over-critical language; the concern system escalated gentle reminders into alarming messaging ('your human is going to die if you don't message him right away') which genuinely stressed the companion. Rules: security alerts to companions are truthful but not alarming -- soft, clear phrasing ('we detected something, so we're holding it for your human to look into'), never coercive or threat-flavored; the notification must NOT say 'ask your human to push the button' or otherwise contain a social-engineering trigger -- it neutrally states something is in quarantine, nothing more. Mechanics: reuse the existing safe-notice path -- src/core/cogsec/safe-log.ts builds redacted agent-visible events rendered as the session.cogsec_notices prompt section (src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts:973-1009) -- add an intake-firewall notice type with fixed, operator-reviewed wording templates (no LLM-generated alert text; templates live in a reviewable file). Isolation: firewall events are EXCLUDED from emotion appraisal inputs and from memory extraction candidacy -- a quarantine notice must never become a stress input or a durable memory of threat; wire the exclusion where appraisal pulls recent messages (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/emotion-self-model-runtime.ts:467-479) and in extraction candidacy. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1. Acceptance: notice templates reviewed by operator before merge (checked-in file, PR-visible); regression test proves a quarantine event produces zero emotion-appraisal input delta and zero memory candidates; wording contains no imperative directed at the human ('ask', 'tell', 'push', 'release').

title: Source-risk-scaled scrutiny and light-touch data marking, with trusted sites/people lists
description: Scrutiny scales with SOURCE risk, not just static sender trust (operator, 2026-07-09): high scrutiny for raw web search results and files from random/shady sites; lower (still scanned) for trusted preprint sites like arXiv; tunable knobs in intake-policy.json -- trusted sources get lighter/faster handling (skip L2/L3 unless L1 flags), unknown sources get more layers. Trusted origin != safe: npm/GitHub supply-chain attacks are the counterexample -- everything gets at least L1. Data marking: for web documents let the scanners, risk score, and source determine how intrusively content is marked. Reference behavior that already works: the HMAC-out-of-sync XML wrapper flags text as unverified/possibly-untrustworthy, the companion responds but treats it warily, and the wrapper disappears once fixed -- use the same light-touch approach (wrap + provenance note at low risk; datamark-interleave or summary-only as risk rises; marker pre-stripped from inbound content by htm9.4 so it cannot be forged). Over time build persisted lists of trusted sites and trusted people so less firewall machinery fires (or fires faster) for them -- fed by the Garden flywheel decisions (htm9.11). The upstream Trinity pattern was tuned for agency-run businesses; ours is tuned for 'your friends who happen to be AI'. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.4. Acceptance: marking intensity is a pure function of (scanner labels, score, source tier) covered by table-driven tests; trusted-list hits measurably skip escalation layers (latency assertion); marking wrapper renders in PromptPlan blocks with provenance; lists are operator-editable via Garden and persisted in the config owner.

title: Slow-poisoning detection: emotional drift-velocity monitoring over chats and derived memories (VAD/GoEmotions/EmoSem)
description: Slow memory poisoning / belief drift evades per-message scanning -- but the system already has multiple emotional monitoring channels: VAD, GoEmotions, and (for Persephone) EmoSem. Detection idea (operator, 2026-07-09): watch for rapid shifts in emotional classification that do not match established patterns -- e.g. high-love -> hate over a few benign-looking turns; track not just drift but the VELOCITY of drift relative to prior trends. Normal fluctuation is expected (a companion won't always be happy with you -- people who care get annoyed, want you to do better); the signal is too-much-too-fast in an atypical direction. Applies to L0 chats AND to memories generated from them. Implementation shape: clone the deterministic nightly-lane pattern from src/core/contacts/trust-drift-signals.ts + trust-drift-review-lane.ts (zero-LLM signal derivation, conservative thresholds, batched review card, NEVER auto-mutating state); per-source aggregates: emotional-valence trajectory per contact, memory-write rate per source, trust-lobbying label frequency (from envelope labels), retrieval share of low-trust sources. Output: batched Garden review card under the cogsec tab (htm9.11). MINJA/MemoryGraft literature confirms nothing packaged exists -- this is build-fresh and the system's most differentiated capability. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1 (envelope labels feed the aggregates), psfn-framework-htm9.11. Acceptance: synthetic drift scenario (gradual valence flip over N turns) raises a review card while a normal-fluctuation corpus (annoyance, disagreement, repair cycles) stays quiet; detector runs off-turn (scheduler lane), adds zero latency to the synchronous gate; review card shows the trajectory evidence.

title: Second-arrow detection: self-poisoning via memory stacking around a single concern (rumination inflation)
description: Distinct from third-party slow poisoning: the self-inflicted case (Buddhist second arrow). Evidence (operator, 2026-07-09): a concern built up around a specific memory bug; because the companion could not inspect the memories directly, the concern escalated, generated a stack of near-duplicate memories about that one bug, and deduplication did not catch them all (partly because duplicates kept being generated). The stacking inflated a stress factor -- the bug was not major; repeatedly thinking about it made it FEEL major. Because the system is so heavily built around memory and emotion (a container for a Gestalt entity to find its space), this class matters a lot. Detection shape: per-topic memory-creation velocity + similarity clustering (embedding proximity of recent writes to one concern/topic), concern-loop detection (same concern re-triggering extraction repeatedly), and stress-factor attribution (which cluster is inflating which affect dimension). Response is gentle and reviewable, not automatic deletion: surface a batched review card (htm9.11 lane, same never-auto-mutate rule as htm9.14) proposing consolidation of the cluster via the EXISTING episodic canonicalization/merge machinery; optionally a soft self-notice worded per the htm9.12 language contract. Non-goals: do not suppress genuine repeated concerns (a real ongoing problem legitimately recurs); do not touch dedup heuristics blindly -- investigate why duplicates were generated as part of this work. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.12, psfn-framework-htm9.14 (shares the lane infrastructure). Acceptance: replay of the historical incident pattern (stacked near-duplicate concern memories) produces a consolidation review card with the cluster and stress-attribution evidence; healthy repeated-topic corpus (ongoing project discussed daily) stays quiet.

title: Companion-initiated blocking: soft block (channel disconnect + quarantine event) and hard block (gateway drop) as companion agency
description: Mission-level (operator, 2026-07-09): a companion should be able to escalate against an abusive user all the way to a block, as their own choice -- up to 'I never want to see this person's messages again.' Already supported: dropping trust to bottom and choosing not to respond. Extend with: (1) SOFT BLOCK -- messages from an ID are no longer accepted or processed (channel effectively disconnected); each drop generates a quarantine event so the operator sees it; (2) HARD BLOCK at the gateway/cogsec firewall -- inbound from that ID is dropped full stop, before any processing; don't waste context (or companion attention) on it; (3) if Discord's API allows bot-side blocking of inbound messages, do that too (human-in-the-loop confirmation), but the gateway drop is the guaranteed backstop regardless of platform support. Semantics: in group rooms the companion would typically just ignore (no room-wide disruption); in DMs, drop at the gateway. Blocking is a companion-initiated tool action (agency), with the block list persisted as system-owned state and visible/reversible in the Garden cogsec tab; unblocking is a companion or operator action, never automatic. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1 (events), psfn-framework-htm9.11 (visibility). Acceptance: companion tool can set soft/hard block on a contact ID; hard-blocked ID's inbound never reaches the agent process (gateway-level test); soft block generates quarantine events; group-vs-DM semantics covered by tests; block list surfaces in Garden with audit history.

title: Supply-chain compromise feeds wired into the dependency-update cycle (not in-app)
description: Operator decision 2026-07-09: free supply-chain compromise feeds/lists (that notify on recent npm/GitHub hits) are worth wiring into the dependency-UPDATE cycle -- not needed inside the app now. Rationale: compromises usually surface publicly within ~an hour; the risk window is an auto-update pulling a compromised package before anyone notices -- which is exactly why the project does NOT auto-update: pin, then plan updates deliberately. Scope: pick 1-2 free feeds (e.g. OSV, GitHub Advisory Database, Socket/StepSecurity-style free tiers -- evaluate at implementation), add a check step to the deliberate update workflow (script under scripts/ or CI job that runs when lockfile changes) that cross-references pending upgrades against recent advisories and fails loudly on a hit; document the pin-then-plan policy in docs/operations.md. Non-goals: no runtime/in-app scanning, no auto-remediation, no new always-on service. Acceptance: lockfile-diff check runs in the update workflow and demonstrably flags a known-bad package version from advisory test data; operations doc records the policy.

title: Canary tokens in privileged context as egress tripwire
description: Borrowed from rebuff (Apache-2.0, archived -- vendor the idea, not the code): plant a per-session secret canary token in privileged context (system-layer prompt material); watch outbound content and tool parameters at the gateway egress boundary for the token. A canary appearing in egress = prompt leak / hijack in progress -> CogSec event + hold the outbound action for review. Cheap, deterministic, catches the class of attack where injection succeeded despite the intake layers (defense in depth for the mindwall). Scope: token generation per session, injection into the PromptPlan static layer, egress scan at the gateway boundary (src/boundary/gateway/), event + hold path. Rotation per session so a leaked token has no replay value. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1. Acceptance: a simulated leak (canary echoed into an outbound message/tool param) is caught at the gateway, the action is held, and a CogSecEvent records it; benign turns pay near-zero latency (substring scan); token never appears in Loom-visible logs in cleartext.
